things.name: the de Grey family's time at Wrest
things.who: the Greys: barons, then Earls of Kent from 1465, then the Duke of Kent, Jemima, Marchioness Grey, Amabel, Countess de Grey, and the 2nd Earl de Grey, then his Cowper and Lucas heirs, until the estate was sold in 1917

things.name: the first record of the Greys at Wrest
things.who: of Reginald de Grey holding one fee in Flitton and Silsoe of John de Wahull; papers made at his death in 1307–1308 list a 'capital messuage with a dovecote', thought to be the beginning of the house

things.name: Edmund Grey's creation as Earl of Kent
things.who: Edward IV's reward to Edmund Grey, who had changed to the Yorkist side at the Battle of Northampton in 1460 and was made Lord High Treasurer in 1463

things.name: Richard Grey's sale of Wrest to Sir Henry Wyatt
things.who: forced on Richard Grey, 3rd Earl of Kent, by his debts (the date is from the Inventories of Bedfordshire Country Houses; a deed of 1514 calls it a mortgage)

things.name: Henry Grey's buying back of Wrest
things.who: done by Sir Henry Grey, Richard's half-brother, who feared Wyatt would pull the house down; he paid 450 marks (£300). Bedfordshire Archives also gives 28 April 1514

things.name: Reginald Grey's recognition as Earl of Kent
things.who: granted by Elizabeth I, after the title had 'lain asleep' for about fifty years because Henry Grey could not afford to take it

things.name: the creation of the barony of Lucas of Crudwell
things.who: made for Mary, wife of Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, by Charles II, with a rule that let it pass through women; this is how Wrest later passed to Jemima, Amabel and Anne Florence

things.name: Jemima's inheritance of Wrest
things.who: when Henry, Duke of Kent, died on 5 June 1740 with no surviving son; she had married Philip Yorke two weeks earlier, on 22 May 1740

things.name: Thomas, Earl de Grey's inheritance of Wrest
things.who: from his aunt Amabel, Countess de Grey, who died on 4 March 1833 (Bedfordshire Archives says 4 May)

things.name: Whitelaw Reid's tenancy of Wrest
things.who: the American ambassador, who rented Wrest from Lord Lucas at £1,500 a year from 1905 and stayed about eight years

things.name: King Edward VII's visit to Wrest
things.who: a weekend visit on 24–25 July 1909 as the guest of the ambassador Whitelaw Reid; the Bedfordshire Times called it the first visit by a sovereign to Wrest

things.name: the First World War hospital at Wrest
things.who: set up by Nan Herbert and her brother Lord Lucas, who paid for it; ready for patients on 7 September 1914 and about 1,600 men passed through

things.name: the 1916 fire at Wrest
things.who: on 14 September 1916; it badly damaged the mansion (a local account puts it in the east wing), all 156 patients were got out safely and the hospital never reopened

things.name: the sale of Wrest
things.who: put up for sale by Nan Herbert, Baroness Lucas, after her brother Auberon was killed in 1916 and the house was damaged by fire; the buyer was John George Murray of Thirsk, a brewery and coal company chairman, in a private sale

things.name: the 1917 auction of Wrest's contents
things.who: run on the premises by Messrs Foster from 10 September 1917 for five days

things.name: the sale of Wrest's statues under John George Murray
things.who: carried out in the 1930s by Murray, who moved to Coles Park in 1933; the Four Seasons and Four Elements went to Ditchley Park and the Duke's obelisk and the Duchess's column to Trent Park

things.name: English Heritage's takeover of Wrest
things.who: after the Silsoe Research Institute closed at the end of March 2006; English Heritage began a 20-year restoration plan

things.name: the reopening of the restored gardens
things.who: on 4 August 2011, after restoration helped by the Heritage Lottery Fund and the Wolfson Foundation

things.name: English Heritage's archaeological collections store
things.who: a £2 million purpose-built store holding over 150,000 objects from English Heritage sites, opened to visitors in 2014
